draft.title: Social structures in the pre-modern world
card: Most pre-modern societies were ranked. People belonged to groups, and each group had a different level of power, wealth and respect.
Rulers and nobles sat at the top. They held most of the land, power and wealth.
Peasants, who farmed the land, and enslaved people, who were forced to work and owned by others, sat at the bottom. They had little power.
Your place usually came from the family you were born into. Few people could move up or down. In medieval Europe, for example, a peasant's child usually stayed a peasant.
draft.remember: Pre-modern societies were ranked, and most people stayed in the place they were born into.

a.q: Why was it hard for a peasant's child in a pre-modern society to become a noble?
opts: Place in society mostly came from birth, so it rarely changed
Peasants were not allowed to farm any land
Nobles were chosen by the vote of the peasants
Every person was born into the same rank
a.why: Rank usually came from the family a person was born into, so few could change their place. The other options are wrong because peasants did farm land, and societies were ranked, not equal.
a.clue: Think about how a person's place was decided.

b.q: In a medieval society, Aldric is a lord who owns a large estate. Brida farms a small plot on his land. Where did each most likely sit in the ranking?
opts: Aldric near the top, Brida near the bottom
Aldric near the bottom, Brida near the top
Both near the top, as both held land
Both in the middle, as ranks were equal
b.why: Nobles such as lords held most land and power, so Aldric sat near the top. Peasants such as Brida farmed the land and had little power. Brida using land did not make her a noble.
b.clue: Who held the land and power, and who worked it?

proposal.title: Social structures in the pre-modern world
card: Most pre-modern societies were ranked. People belonged to groups, and each group had a different level of power, wealth and respect.
Rulers and nobles sat at the top. They held most of the land, power and wealth.
Peasants, who farmed the land, and enslaved people, who were forced to work and owned by others, sat at the bottom. They had little power.
Your place usually came from the family you were born into, not from your work or savings. Few people could move up or down. In medieval Europe, a peasant's child usually stayed a peasant.
proposal.remember: Pre-modern societies were ranked, and most people stayed in the place they were born into.

a.q: Tomas, a peasant's son in medieval Europe, works hard and saves some money. Why does he most likely stay a peasant?
opts: His rank came mainly from the family he was born into
His rank came mainly from the money he had saved up
His rank came mainly from how hard he worked each day
His rank came mainly from a vote by people in his village
a.why: In most pre-modern societies, a person's place usually came from the family they were born into, so few could move up. Hard work or savings rarely changed that, which is why Tomas most likely stays a peasant like his parents.
a.clue: Think about what was fixed for Tomas before he did any work.
